subject: SS
title: Old, Middle and New Kingdoms
teach: The Old Kingdom is strongly associated with large royal pyramids. Khufu is the pharaoh associated with the Great Pyramid at Giza.
Large building projects required planning, supplies and many workers with different skills. A monument is evidence of organized work as well as royal power.

Do not mix up the builders: Khufu is associated with the Great Pyramid; Imhotep is associated with Djoser’s earlier Step Pyramid. The textbook’s construction numbers and some names are unreliable, so use the well-supported ruler-and-monument link.
After the Old Kingdom, Egypt experienced periods of divided power. Mentuhotep II reunited Egypt. Historians connect this reunification with the beginning of the Middle Kingdom.
Reunite means bring together again. Menes and Mentuhotep II are not interchangeable: the classroom account links Menes with early unification and Mentuhotep II with a later reunification.
Learn the order rather than the textbook’s conflicting date ranges: Old Kingdom → divided rule → Mentuhotep II and the Middle Kingdom.
The Hyksos were rulers with origins in western Asia who controlled northern Egypt for part of the Second Intermediate Period. They were not one of Egypt’s three kingdom names.
Ahmose I led the defeat of Hyksos rule and helped reunify Egypt. He is connected with the start of the New Kingdom.

Remember the change: Hyksos rule in the north → Ahmose defeats their rule → New Kingdom. The textbook’s claim about iron weapons is misleading; the important tested connection is the change in rulers, not that claim.

It proves every worker had the same social rank.
It proves one ruler built it without help.
delayed.rationale: Correct: It can show royal power and organized work. Do not mix up the builders: Khufu is associated with the Great Pyramid; Imhotep is associated with Djoser’s earlier Step Pyramid. The textbook’s construction numbers and some names are unreliable, so use the well-supported ruler-and-monument link.

Papyrus and writing
Ramses II at Abu Simbel

repair.prompt: If a reading says a ruler restored unity, what should you look for?
options: Evidence of divided rule followed by shared rule
Evidence that the Nile changed direction
Evidence that all occupations disappeared.
repair.rationale: Correct: Evidence of divided rule followed by shared rule. After the Old Kingdom, Egypt experienced periods of divided power. Mentuhotep II reunited Egypt. Historians connect this reunification with the beginning of the Middle Kingdom. Reunite means bring together again. Menes and Mentuhotep II are not interchangeable: the classroom account links Menes with early unification and Mentuhotep II with a later reunification. Learn the order rather than the textbook’s conflicting date ranges: Old Kingdom → divided rule → Mentuhotep II and the Middle Kingdom.

delayed.prompt: Which order fits the assigned history?
options: Hyksos rule → Ahmose’s victory → New Kingdom
New Kingdom → Khufu’s pyramid → Hyksos rule
Ahmose’s victory → Menes’s early unification → Old Kingdom
delayed.rationale: Correct: Hyksos rule → Ahmose’s victory → New Kingdom. Remember the change: Hyksos rule in the north → Ahmose defeats their rule → New Kingdom. The textbook’s claim about iron weapons is misleading; the important tested connection is the change in rulers, not that claim.

repair.prompt: Why should you connect Ahmose to an event, not only memorize his name?
options: The event explains his role in the change to New Kingdom rule.
His name tells you the Nile’s length.
Every ruler had exactly the same role.
repair.rationale: Correct: The event explains his role in the change to New Kingdom rule. The Hyksos were rulers with origins in western Asia who controlled northern Egypt for part of the Second Intermediate Period. They were not one of Egypt’s three kingdom names. Ahmose I led the defeat of Hyksos rule and helped reunify Egypt. He is connected with the start of the New Kingdom. Remember the change: Hyksos rule in the north → Ahmose defeats their rule → New Kingdom. The textbook’s claim about iron weapons is misleading; the important tested connection is the change in rulers, not that claim.
